source_refs.note: Exercise 2.1, Question 10: differentiate y = sqrt(sin x) + cos sqrt(x); book p. 41. Unit 2 has no printed answers.

blocks.prompt: 10. Differentiate w.r.t. the variable involved: \(y = \sqrt{\sin x} + \cos\sqrt{x}\)
blocks.explanation:
Two composite terms with the layers in opposite order.
\(\sqrt{\sin x}\): root outside, \(\sin x\) inside. \(\cos\sqrt{x}\): cosine outside, \(\sqrt{x}\) inside.
Plan: chain rule on each term separately, then add.
steps:
Given: \(y = \sqrt{\sin x} + \cos\sqrt{x}\), with \(x > 0\), \(\sin x > 0\).
To find: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Method: sum rule, then the chain rule ('derivative of the outer, times derivative of the inner') on each term.

First term: root of sin x
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x)^{1/2} = \tfrac{1}{2}(\sin x)^{-1/2}\cos x\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}\]
Why: outer \(u^{1/2}\) with \(u = \sin x\), \(\frac{du}{dx} = \cos x\).

Second term: cos of root x
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\cos\sqrt{x} = -\sin\sqrt{x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
Why: outer \(\cos w\) with \(w = \sqrt{x}\), \(\frac{dw}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\).

Add
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}} - \dfrac{\sin\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
Why: sum rule.

Check at x = pi/2
\[\dfrac{0}{2} - \dfrac{\sin\sqrt{\pi/2}}{2\sqrt{\pi/2}} \approx -0.379\]
Why: \(\sqrt{\sin x}\) has its peak at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) (slope 0), so only the \(\cos\sqrt{x}\) part contributes, and \(\cos\sqrt{x}\) is decreasing there.
